test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 23 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The profit made on a product is 79%. What is the loss percentage (correct to two 3 decimal places) incurred on the sale if the figures of both the cost price and the selling price are interchanged?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume **Cost Price (CP)** = 100. Then **Selling Price (SP)** = 179.

When CP and SP are **interchanged**, New CP = 179 and New SP = 100.

Loss = 179 − 100 = 79.

**Loss%** = (79 ÷ 179) × 100.

Calculation: 7900 ÷ 179 ≈ 44.134%.

**∴ The correct answer is 44.13%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Profit = 79%, New CP = Old SP, New SP = Old CP.

**Formulas:** SP = CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100 | Loss% = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a51efa27abb01c8e2e9dd55473b5e12651be9fd53cc14b38da985f4f0db326d8.png] 

⇒ Let **Initial Cost Price (CP₁)** = 100 units.

⇒ Initial Profit = 79%, so **Initial Selling Price (SP₁)** = 179 units.

⇒ After interchanging, **New Cost Price (CP₂)** = 179 units and **New Selling Price (SP₂)** = 100 units.

⇒ New Loss = CP₂ − SP₂ = 179 − 100 = 79 units.

⇒ **Loss Percentage** = (Loss ÷ CP₂) × 100 = (79 ÷ 179) × 100.

⇒ Loss% = 44.13407...% ≈ 44.13%.

**∴ The correct answer is 44.13%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit or Loss is always calculated on the **Cost Price** unless specified otherwise. Formula: Profit% = (P/CP)×100 and Loss% = (L/CP)×100.

Interchanging CP and SP

If a transaction results in a profit, interchanging CP and SP will always result in a loss. The **absolute value** of the profit/loss remains the same, but the **percentage** changes because the base (CP) changes.</p
